guide.summary: Internal use, your own Zendesk account (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Multi-customer app (global OAuth client) (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Internal use, your own Zendesk account (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).

composio.note: Composio lists a managed OAuth app for Zendesk, fine for prototypes. For launch use your own client ID and secret in a Composio auth config.

need_own_app.answer: For a prototype, Composio's managed app works. For production across multiple Zendesk customers, you need your own client, and Zendesk requires a global OAuth client that it creates for you.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Managed apps share rate-limit quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval
Default scopes may not cover what you need
Zendesk requires global OAuth tokens for apps used across multiple customers

prerequisites.title: Zendesk admin account
prerequisites.detail: An admin must create the OAuth client.

prerequisites.title: Sponsored developer account (d3v-)
prerequisites.detail: The global client request is only accepted from accounts with the d3v- prefix.

prerequisites.title: Registered organization on Marketplace portal
prerequisites.detail: Register your organization at apps.zendesk.com before submitting.

steps.title: Create local OAuth client in Admin Center
steps.detail: Sign in as admin, set Client kind to Confidential, add the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard, and save the Identifier and Secret.
steps.done_when: You have the client Identifier and Secret saved securely.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Zendesk auth config through Composio's API using your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection works.

steps.title: Limit scopes to what you need
steps.detail: Draft the minimal scope list and set it as the client's allowed scopes.
inputs: List of API calls the agent makes
steps.done_when: Allowed scopes match the agent's needs.

steps.title: Request global OAuth client
steps.detail: Note the client secret and identifier first. In the Marketplace portal, choose Global OAuth, then Request new OAuth, and complete every field.
steps.done_when: You receive an email and ticket reference.

steps.title: Prepare and submit Marketplace app
steps.detail: Upload the source ZIP, answer the compliance question, and accept the terms. For an integration app, include marketing assets, translations and a manifest.
steps.done_when: The form submits without automatic check errors.

steps.title: Wait for Zendesk review
steps.detail: New submissions take 1-3 weeks. If rejected, resubmit a corrected ZIP with Submit Update.

steps.title: Share preview link or publish
steps.detail: For a preview app, add customer accounts on the Availability tab and share the link. To go public, submit an update asking for publication.

traps.title: Client access is lost after conversion
traps.detail: Once the local client becomes global, you lose the client admin page, so save the secret and identifier beforehand. The identifier should be the exact production value.

traps.title: Regular tokens are not allowed for multi-customer apps
traps.detail: Customers may not share regular API or OAuth tokens with you, so apps for many customers must use global tokens.

traps.title: Scopes outside the allowed list fail
traps.detail: A requested scope outside the allowed scopes returns 400 invalid_scope and no token. Only Zendesk can edit a global client, so scope changes go through Zendesk Support.

traps.title: Optional fields are required
traps.detail: Even fields labeled optional must be completed for global clients, and non-d3v- submissions are rejected.

traps.title: Global client does not cover Sell or bots
traps.detail: The process applies only to Zendesk Support and Chat (Agent Workspace enabled). Sell needs a Multi-User Application, and Sunshine Conversations bots need a separate token.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: The redirect URI in the authorization request must exactly match the client's registered value.

blockers.what_it_means: The app requested a scope not in the client's allowed scopes.
blockers.what_to_do: Request only allowed scopes, or edit the client's allowed scopes (via Zendesk Support for global clients).
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes with the allowed list.

blockers.what_it_means: The automatic check of the ZIP found errors.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix the errors; warnings are only suggestions.
blockers.agent_can_help: Review the ZIP contents and manifest against the errors.

blockers.what_it_means: Zendesk did not approve the submission.
blockers.what_to_do: Upload a corrected ZIP with Submit Update under the original submission.

open_questions: Which scopes, if any, trigger extra scrutiny? Ask Zendesk Support or see the OAuth scopes page.
